lines.en: Lesson 35
lines.zh: 第35课

lines.en: Space odyssey
lines.zh: 太空漫游

lines.en: When will it be possible for us to think seriously about colonising Mars?
lines.zh: 我们什么时候才能认真考虑在火星上殖民？

lines.en: The Moon is likely to become the industrial hub of the Solar System supplying the rocket fuels for its ships,
lines.zh: 月球很可能成为太阳系的工业中心，为其飞船提供火箭燃料，

lines.en: easily obtainable from the lunar rocks in the form of liquid oxygen.
lines.zh: 这些燃料以液氧的形式，可轻易地从月球岩石中获得。

lines.en: The reason lies in its gravity.
lines.zh: 原因在于它的重力。

lines.en: Because the Moon has only an eightieth of the Earth's mass,
lines.zh: 因为月球的质量只有地球的八十分之一，

lines.en: it requires 97% less energy
lines.zh: 它所需的能量要少97%，

lines.en: to travel the quarter of a million miles from the Moon to Earth-orbit than the 200 mile-journey from Earth's surface into orbit!
lines.zh: 即使是从月球到地球轨道25万英里的旅程，也比从地球表面进入轨道200英里的旅程所需的能量少得多！

lines.en: This may sound fantastic, but it is easily calculated.
lines.zh: 这听起来可能很不可思议，但它很容易计算出来。

lines.en: To escape from the Earth in a rocket, one must travel at seven miles per second.
lines.zh: 要乘坐火箭逃离地球，必须以每秒7英里的速度飞行。

lines.en: The comparable speed from the Moon is only 1.5 miles per second.
lines.zh: 而从月球逃离的可比速度仅为每秒1.5英里。

lines.en: Because the gravity on the Moon's surface is only a sixth of Earth's (remember how easily the Apollo astronauts bounded along),
lines.zh: 因为月球表面的重力只有地球的六分之一（还记得阿波罗宇航员在月球上跳跃得多轻松吗？），

lines.en: it takes much less energy to accelerate to that 1.5mps than it does on Earth.
lines.zh: 因此，在月球上加速到每秒1.5英里所需的能量比在地球上少得多。

lines.en: Moon dwellers will be able to fly in space at only three percent of the cost of similar journeys by their terrestrial cousins.
lines.zh: 月球居民将能够以其地球表亲进行类似旅程所需成本的3%在太空中飞行。

lines.en: Arthur C.Clark once suggested a revolutionary idea passes through three phases:
lines.zh: 亚瑟·C·克拉克曾提出，一个革命性的想法会经历三个阶段：

lines.en: 1.  'It's impossible--don't waste my time.'
lines.zh: 1. “这不可能——别浪费我的时间。”

lines.en: 2.  'It's possible, but not worth doing.'
lines.zh: 2. “这有可能，但不值得做。”

lines.en: 3.  'I said it was a good idea all along.'
lines.zh: 3. “我一直都说这是个好主意。”

lines.en: The idea of colonising Mars--a world 160 times more distant than the Moon--will move decisively from the second phase to the third,
lines.zh: 殖民火星——一个比月球远160倍的世界——的设想，将决定性地从第二阶段迈向第三阶段，

lines.en: when a significant number of people are living permanently in space.
lines.zh: 那将是当大量人口永久居住在太空中的时候。

lines.en: Mars has an extraordinary fascination for would-be voyagers.
lines.zh: 火星对未来的航海家们有着非凡的吸引力。

lines.en: America, Russia and Europe are filled with enthusiasts--many of them serious and senior scientists who dream of sending people to it.
lines.zh: 美国、俄罗斯和欧洲都充满了热情的人士——其中许多是认真而资深的科学家，他们梦想着将人类送上火星。

lines.en: Their aim is understandable.
lines.zh: 他们的目标是可以理解的。

lines.en: It is the one world in the Solar System that is most like the Earth.
lines.zh: 它是太阳系中与地球最相似的星球。

lines.en: It is a world of red sandy deserts (hence its name--the Red Planet),
lines.zh: 这是一个红色的沙质沙漠世界（因此得名——红色星球），

lines.en: cloudless skies, savage sandstorms, chasms wider than the Grand Canyon and at least one mountain more than twice as tall as Everest.
lines.zh: 有着无云的天空、狂暴的沙尘暴、比大峡谷还宽的裂谷，以及至少一座比珠穆朗玛峰高两倍多的山峰。

lines.en: It seems ideal for settlement.
lines.zh: 它似乎非常适合居住。
